_instructions: One entry per industry page. All of these render from a single template at src/pages/[slug].astro. To add an industry, copy an entry and change the values — do not create a new page file. Slugs must match the live site exactly. faqs: three questions per industry, rendered on that page and emitted as FAQPage schema. They must stay UNIQUE per page — the same Q&A repeated across industries is duplicate content and Google ignores duplicated FAQPage markup. Every answer must be supported by something already on that page (a pain point, a system, the recommended plan) or by a figure in pricing.json. If a price changes in pricing.json, grep here for the old figure: these answers quote prices in prose and will not update themselves.

industries.meta_title: Brewery & Taproom POS System | EPAY POS
industries.meta_description: POS for breweries and taprooms — tabs, pours by size, taplist changes mid-shift, and retail can sales on the same ticket.
industries.headline: Tabs, Pours and a Taplist That Changes Weekly
industries.subhead: A taproom is a bar, a retail counter and a production schedule at once. The catalog has to change as fast as the taplist.

faqs.q: How do you keep a changing taplist current on the POS?
faqs.a: Edit the catalog from anywhere and the change is live on every terminal at once, so the menu is not out of date by Friday.

faqs.q: Can you track pour sizes and flights properly?
faqs.a: Size-based pricing and flights as real items mean depletion actually tracks, rather than every pour being rung as one generic item.

faqs.q: Can merch and to-go cans go on the same ticket as the taproom?
faqs.a: Yes. Retail inventory sits on the same ticket as the taproom, so merch and to-go cans are not rung on a separate system.

pain_points.problem: The taplist changes and the menu is out of date by Friday.
pain_points.solution: Edit the catalog from anywhere; the change is live on every terminal at once.

pain_points.problem: Pour sizes and flights are rung as one generic item.
pain_points.solution: Size-based pricing and flights as real items, so depletion actually tracks.

pain_points.problem: Merch and to-go cans get rung on a separate system.
pain_points.solution: Retail inventory on the same ticket as the taproom.

industries.headline: The Front of the Store, Run Properly

faqs.q: How does a pharmacy POS handle front-of-store inventory?
faqs.a: Real-time counts with low-stock alerts cover every SKU in the aisles, instead of front-of-store stock being counted by hand.

faqs.q: Does it prompt for age-restricted items?

pain_points.problem: Age-restricted items rely on staff remembering.
pain_points.solution: ID scanning and prompts at the register on the items that need it.

pain_points.problem: Two registers hold two different prices.
pain_points.solution: One catalog, pushed to every terminal at once.

industries.meta_description: POS for boutiques and apparel — size and color variants, one catalog across the shop floor and the online store, and inventory that stays honest.
industries.headline: Size, Color and One Honest Stock Count
industries.subhead: Apparel is the same product eight times over. The system has to know a medium in black is not a large in navy, on the shop floor and online at the same time.

faqs.q: How does a boutique POS handle sizes and colours?
faqs.a: Size and colour are real variants, each with its own count, so stock does not go wrong the moment a variant is rung as one item.

faqs.q: Can the shop and the online store share stock?
faqs.a: One catalog sits behind the counter and the storefront, so stock is shared and the website cannot sell something the shop already sold.

faqs.q: How are seasonal markdowns applied?
faqs.a: Promotions and mix-and-match pricing apply at the register automatically, rather than being worked out with a calculator.

pain_points.problem: Variants are rung as one item and stock goes wrong immediately.
pain_points.solution: Size and colour as real variants, each with its own count.

pain_points.problem: The website sells something the shop already sold.
pain_points.solution: One catalog behind the counter and the storefront, so stock is shared.

pain_points.problem: Seasonal markdowns are done with a calculator.
pain_points.solution: Promotions and mix-and-match pricing applied at the register automatically.

pain_points.solution: Customer profiles with purchase history, so the reorder is one lookup.

pain_points.problem: Vendor prices move and margins quietly slip.
pain_points.solution: Purchase orders and vendor cost tracking, so a cost change is visible.

faqs.q: How are tips handled across a team?

faqs.q: Can you track retail product sales separately from services?
faqs.a: Services and products ring on the same ticket, with real inventory on the retail lines, so you can see what sells off the shelf. The plan for a salon is EPAY Table Mobile at $39.99 a month.

pain_points.problem: Bookings live in one app and payment in another.
pain_points.solution: Appointments and checkout in the same place, so the ticket is already open when they walk to the desk.

pain_points.problem: Tips across a team are a spreadsheet at the end of the week.
pain_points.solution: Tip handling and pooling on the system, per staff member, per shift.

pain_points.problem: Retail product sales get lost against services.
pain_points.solution: Real inventory on retail lines, so you know what sells off the shelf.

_note_on_images: Every industry page expects one hero image and three gallery shots. Drop the files at the paths in hero_image / gallery and each slot renders the real photo automatically. Until then the slot shows the filename it wants. Real photography only — no stock shots of people shaking hands, per design-system.md.
_note_on_systems: The three system blocks per industry, worded from the live epaypos.net restaurant and retail pages. Restaurant gets the kitchen order screen; retail gets the customer facing display.
_note_on_new_verticals: Quick Service, Food Truck, Fine Dining, Brewery & Taproom, Salon & Spa, Pharmacy, Boutique & Apparel and Pet Supply were added in this build. Their copy is written from how those businesses operate — no statistics, no named customers, no case studies. Salon & Spa is filed under retail because the site has two categories; it is the natural home for the nail-salon POS.
_note_on_home: `on_home` controls the 'Built per business type' list on the homepage — the original 11 verticals only. The eight added later still have full pages and still appear in the Restaurant and Retail mega-menus; they are just not on that homepage list. Flip on_home to show one.
_note_on_salon: Salon & Spa was removed — that vertical is being built out later, alongside the nail-salon POS. Nothing else referenced it, so removing the entry removed the page.
_note_on_services: Auto, home and professional services sit under retail because the site has two categories — they are service businesses whose hook is invoicing and payment links, not a register. Salon & Spa carries coming_soon: true, which renders a banner and softens the CTAs on that page only.
